pre_mortem: It's Monday and both legs lost. Wilson finished under 75.5 because Chicago did not blitz at the 42% rate once it led on the ground, his 284 air yards were taken away, and targets leaked to Sadiq (already 14 targets, 143 yards) and Hall (10 targets, 102 yards); an 81-yard three-game average is only a 5.5-yard cushion. Swift finished under 64.5 because the committee is already in the pack — Monangai 30 carries at 5.93 YPC and Caleb Williams 15 carries at 7.13 YPC — and if Chicago threw toward Burden (23 targets) and Raymond (21 targets), Swift slid to about 12 carries, and 12 times NYJ's 4.40 YPC allowed is 52.8. A late snap limit would do the same, and no injury report was in the pack. The counter-case is real but not stronger than the read: Swift still led CHI with 54 carries and Wilson still led NYJ with 28 targets into a defense allowing 7-plus YPA on every side.
slip_story: One story: CHI runs, NYJ throws. Swift rushyds over 64.5 and Wilson recyds over 75.5 win together if Chicago controls pace on the ground and New York, stuck at 3.2 YPC with Hall, has to throw. Do not add CHI receiver overs or NYJ rusher overs; those need the opposite flip. No TD legs. One market per player. Main slip is these two correlated legs only.
